data.text: ADR-010 coupled-phase assessment: the initial fence repair made every Progress::StateChange failure reload and write final state. The live provider-outcome test fails in retained_boundaries::reconciliation (live-diagnostic-6.log); source confirms an ordinary RetryDeferred from renew_dispatch_possible_after_absence reaches this fallback and changes a row that the existing test requires unchanged. Core/PhasedJob already retain concrete failure versus interruption/panic. Cause: application provider-policy distinction, not missing library ownership. Remedy within authorized scope: preserve concrete returned fence failures without inventing a budget interruption; use reload/finalization only when work did not return a concrete failure or explicitly returned FenceInterrupted. Alternative of moving provider state policy into core would violate ownership; skipping all StateChange recovery would leave the confirmed deadline race. Retain existing reconciliation test and new real blocked-fence tests; no separate design scope needed. New fixture diagnostics also corrected SELECT-for-update ordering and timer-driver control; these are test assumptions, not product guarantees.

Round 1 repairs submitted to controller bda103d1-ecc9-4e79-a09f-ed310a048efb (balanced/per-round, saved panel import, Claude+Codex). Diagnostic evidence: core phased tests 16 pass; public adapter tests 5 pass; production panic classifier passes; affected all-target/all-feature Clippy passes; API JSON extraction adds only OperationPhases::validate_reserve to the original cutover inventory. Disposable PostgreSQL diagnostic live-diagnostic-7.log passes 68 reference lib tests including ignored fence/maintenance cases, 2 provider outcome/crash-restart cases, and delivery reconciliation. These diagnostics do not replace pinned controller validation; full scripts/verify.sh and live checks now pending. The new committed-fence scenario withholds a work result after a real commit; wire-level acknowledgement loss and fresh-agent feature-task usability are not claimed.

Controller validation passed on repair commit c2b137b: 00007-validate ran bash scripts/verify.sh with exit 0 (format/file budgets, all 4 Clippy configurations, all 6 matrix parts, strict workspace rustdoc, all HTTP smoke profiles); 00008-validate ran the pinned disposable PostgreSQL runner with exit 0 (2 provider outcome/crash-restart cases, delivery reconciliation, 68 reference lib tests including ignored fence and maintenance cases). No matrix rerun is needed. Fresh full-range Claude and Codex reviews are now running as 00009-review and 00010-review against base 986d294 through the repaired tip.

Fresh review wave complete: Codex reports no findings and all criteria satisfied; Claude also confirms all four repairs and all criteria, with one low-severity facade documentation inconsistency at crates/batter/src/lib.rs:45. The selection table still applies into_job_handler() to the canonical PhasedJob, which already implements JobHandler. Triage accepts this stale recipe; correcting the table in a documentation-only repair round. No runtime change or new test is needed; existing executable facade rustdoc already shows the correct direct handler call. Controller retains the completed round-1 validation and reviews and will bind fresh evidence to the final tip.

ADR-010 recurrence assessment before round 3: Codex 00016-review demonstrates a distinct pre-callback deadline window after Bulkhead post-admission check and before OperationContext preflight. Progress remains Admission, but the migrated dispatch consumer maps Operation::Interrupted to Uncertain, which requires ReconcileNeeded and can terminally fail an undispatched row. Source inspection confirms the separate checks and span-construction gap. Earlier StateChange-only repair fixed the pending-fence scenario but left the broader progress-classification cause partially addressed. The available application Progress already distinguishes Preparing, Admission, StateChange, Reconcile and Dispatch; core never promises that Operation::Interrupted proves invocation. Cause: duplicated application protocol interpretation, not missing native ownership or a need for a second worker engine. Bounded remedy: one exhaustive interruption-to-action mapping shared by reconcile, dispatch and finalization; preserve concrete SQL/policy failure handling. Add a real production/PG regression that expires work in admitted operation span creation before callback invocation and verifies no fence/provider start, legal undispatched state and retryable timeout. Alternatives: another one-off Admission guard would leave duplicate policy; changing Bulkhead public semantics would not eliminate application fence/remote-outcome policy and is unnecessary. No scope expansion or separate design task required; original pending-fence and retry-deferral regressions remain required.

Round 3 diagnostic evidence: scoped tracing subscriber reproduces expiry between bulkhead admission and nested OperationContext callback startup; before fix the actual PostgreSQL handler test fails Terminal vs Timeout (before-factory-before.log). Shared exhaustive application progress mapping now serves nested dispatch/reconcile and outer finalization, preserving concrete fence failures. After fix all 68 reference lib tests including ignored fence/maintenance/pre-callback scenarios pass (before-factory-after.log); affected all-target/all-feature Clippy passes. Documentation and ADR-010 recurrence assessment updated. Submitting to controller for full required gates and fresh review; diagnostics are not the final validation receipts.

data.text: ADR-010 assessment: repeated reference-worker repair exposed a library/adapter gap: strict phased success cannot accept an acknowledged settlement of a value returned after the shortened work deadline. User approved explicit, capability-gated late settlement under the original finalization deadline. Ordinary finalization remains strict; cancellation, missing values, application errors and poll/destruction panics cannot recover success. Application Action meaning and native lease/commit uncertainty remain application/native-owned. No second engine or exactly-once claim. Earlier nested Bulkhead provider-loss finding is rejected: run_inner has no post-return check and dispatch has no await after returned provider evidence. Add actual admitted submission transaction coverage and narrow consumer cancellation evidence. Proposed tests remain unexecuted. No code commits or pushes authorized by this implementation request.
